chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: There is no manumission for the believer after death.
Nor is there a deferment of his debt.
Nor is there charity given on his behalf.
Nor is there pilgrimage performed on his behalf.
Unless he had commanded that before his death.
Then that is carried out on his behalf.
ai.seo_question: What acts can be performed on behalf of a deceased Muslim after their death?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s clarification that posthumous acts like Hajj or charity are not automatic but require explicit prior command, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that voluntary acts (nafl) do not transfer to the estate without instruction. This distinction underscores the importance of clear testamentary intent in Shia inheritance law, ensuring that the deceased’s specific wishes guide the execution of their spiritual and financial legacy.
